title: AI | October 9, 2026
summary: A thin, cross-verified edition: one major dispute over the stated reasons for OpenAI researcher dismissals cleared independent-source review. Other collected items were mostly single-link research or product posts.

stories.headline: Fired OpenAI researchers say they were let go for 'prioritising safety'
stories.dek: OpenAI says the dismissals concerned its sensitive-information policies; the researchers describe a safety dispute.
tldr: BBC reports that former OpenAI researchers say they were dismissed for prioritising safety.
OpenAI disputes that account and says the decisions concerned violations of its sensitive-information policies.
Reuters reports that OpenAI said three researchers were fired after an investigation into information handling.

body.text: The accounts differ on the stated reason for the dismissals: the researchers describe a safety disagreement, while OpenAI cites its information-handling rules.
The available reporting establishes the competing explanations but does not independently resolve the underlying personnel dispute.

stories.whyItMatters: The dispute puts internal safety debate and company information controls in the same governance question; the available reports do not establish which account is correct.
stories.editorNote: Coverage is based on contemporaneous reporting; the reason for the dismissals remains disputed.
